# Ealch v2 — Curriculum, Content Plan & Generation Prompt

**Date:** 2026-07-12 · **Scope:** planning only, no build.
**Covers:** the full content system for every learning mode in the app — Beginners' Den lessons, Speaking, Listening/Playlist, Voice Flash, Role Play, Listen & Write (dictation), Sentence Builder, Flashcards, Smart Review, Coach chat, and exam prep (TEF · TCF · DELF/DALF) — from absolute beginner to proficiency.
**Pipeline target:** content rows in **Supabase** (Postgres), audio files in **Cloudflare R2**, generated by an LLM against the master prompt in Part 3.

---

## 0. Where content stands today (audit of the actual code)

Grounding this plan in what exists, so nothing is designed in a vacuum:

| What | Where | State |
|---|---|---|
| Curriculum skeleton | `src/content/curriculum.ts` | Sons (9 units) + A1 (26 units) + A2 (8 units / 31 sub-lessons). **B1, B2, C1 do not exist.** Units are `{title, sub}` only — no IDs, keyed by array index (`'sons-2'`, `'a1-3'`). |
| Full lessons | `src/content/lessons.ts` | Rich `Lesson` type (intro, conjugation table, examples, common errors, audio scripts, quiz). **Only ~3 lessons actually written** (`sons3`, `a1_4`, `a2_1`); every other unit opens nothing. |
| Flashcards | `src/content/index.ts` `deck` | **8 cards total**, one deck, `{fr, en, ex}`. |
| Voice Flash | `vfItems` | **5 items**, icon is a hardcoded union type (`'cup'|'house'|'book'|'sun'|'car'`) — cannot scale without an image/icon pipeline. |
| Role Play | `rpLines` | **1 scenario** (market stall) × 4 levels (A1–B2), 3 fixed turns each. |
| Sentence Builder | `sbWords` | **1 sentence.** |
| Dictation, Speak, Playlist/Player | screens exist | Content is hardcoded inside the screens; no data files at all. |
| Exam prep | `src/content/onboarding.ts` | Exists only as an onboarding goal chip ("TEF, TCF, DELF — with an examiner who interrupts"). No exam content or exam mode anywhere. |
| Supabase schema | `supabase/schema.sql` | `system_config`, `system_prompts`, `profiles`, `review_items`, `sessions`. **No content tables of any kind.** |
| Content delivery | comment in `src/content/index.ts` | "In production this is served by the remote CMS (ContentService)" — **ContentService does not exist.** |
| Audio | app-wide | 100% on-device TTS (`expo-speech`). No stored audio, no R2, no download manifests (Downloads screen is UI-only). Config references `fishAudio`/`fish-1` TTS provider — not wired. |
| Accent setting | `profiles.accent` default `'Parisienne'` | Implies per-accent audio variants — a cost multiplier decision (see Part 4). |

**Conclusion:** the app is a well-built *player* for content that mostly doesn't exist yet, with no schema to hold it and no pipe to deliver it. This document designs all three: the curriculum (Part 1), the content inventory + schema + audio pipeline (Part 2), and the generation prompt system (Part 3). Part 4 lists everything that will break this if not decided first.

---

# Part 1 — The Curriculum

## 1.1 Design principles

1. **CEFR is the spine.** Every unit, item, and audio file is tagged with one CEFR level: `A0` (Sons/pronunciation foundation), `A1`, `A2`, `B1`, `B2`, `C1`. Exams map onto the spine rather than being a separate world — TEF/TCF/DELF tasks are CEFR-levelled items with an `exam` skin.
2. **One unit → every mode.** A unit like *Le passé composé avec avoir* is not "a lesson"; it is a content *bundle*: 1 lesson + 1 flashcard deck + N dictation sentences + N sentence-builder puzzles + 1 roleplay scenario + 1 playlist episode + speaking drills + quiz + review cards. Modes are different lenses on the same unit, which is what makes Smart Review coherent.
3. **Four skills per level, always.** Compréhension orale (listening), compréhension écrite (reading), production orale (speaking), production écrite (writing). Every unit bundle must touch at least CO + PO (this is a speaking-first app); CE + PE ramp up from B1 because that's where the exams demand them.
4. **Keep what exists.** The Sons/A1/A2 unit lists in `curriculum.ts` are good and already shipped in UI. They are adopted as-is (with stable slugs added — see Part 4, issue 1) and extended, not replaced.
5. **Recycle vocabulary deliberately.** Each unit's items must reuse ≥30% vocabulary from earlier units (spaced re-exposure). This is a generation-prompt constraint, not a manual editing task.

## 1.2 The ladder

```
A0  Sons — pronunciation foundation      9 units   (exists)
A1  Survival French                     26 units   (exists)
A2  Independent basics                  31 sub-lessons in 8 blocks (exists)
B1  Autonomy                            32 units   (new — defined below)
B2  Fluency & argument                  28 units   (new — defined below)
C1  Proficiency                         20 units   (new — defined below)
EX  Exam tracks (TEF / TCF / DELF-DALF) overlay on A2–C1 (new)
```

### B1 — Autonomy (32 units, 4 blocks)

**Block 1 · Le récit (telling stories)** — imparfait vs passé composé; plus-que-parfait; narrative connectors (d'abord, ensuite, du coup); reported speech (present); telling an anecdote; describing a past experience for an exam jury.
**Block 2 · Le futur & les projets** — futur simple; futur vs futur proche; conditionnel présent (politeness & hypothesis); si + imparfait; making plans, promises, predictions; job interviews & career talk.
**Block 3 · L'opinion & l'argument** — subjonctif présent (triggers: il faut que, bien que, vouloir que); opinion verbs + indicative vs subjunctive; agreeing/disagreeing politely; comparing options; complaint letters & service disputes; media & news vocabulary.
**Block 4 · La vie pratique avancée** — relative pronouns (qui/que/dont/où); pronoun stacking (le lui, m'y, en); gérondif; administrative French (préfecture, CAF, bail, mutuelle) — *the immigration-goal killer feature*; health & emergencies in depth; work meetings & small talk.

### B2 — Fluency & argument (28 units, 4 blocks)

**Block 1 · Nuance du temps** — subjonctif passé; conditionnel passé (regret, reproach); concordance des temps; passive voice; participe présent vs gérondif; nominalisation (press style).
**Block 2 · Le débat** — structured argumentation (thèse/antithèse/synthèse); concession & opposition (bien que, malgré, pourtant, en revanche); cause & consequence registers; hedging & emphasis; debating current affairs; the DELF B2 monologue suivi format.
**Block 3 · Registres** — soutenu vs courant vs familier; slang & verlan (recognition); politeness strategies & softeners; email registers (pro vs perso); irony & humour markers; interruptions & repair ("ce que je veux dire, c'est…").
**Block 4 · La France en VO** — fast native speech & reductions (chais pas, y'a); regional accents (recognition: Québec, Midi, Belgique); radio & podcast comprehension; film & series French; workplace culture; French humour & references.

### C1 — Proficiency (20 units, 3 blocks)

**Block 1 · La langue précise** — rare tenses in the wild (passé simple recognition, subjonctif imparfait recognition); stylistic inversion; cleft sentences (c'est…qui/que); idiomatic prepositions; collocations & fixed expressions; false friends at C-level.
**Block 2 · Le discours construit** — synthèse de documents (DALF C1 core task); exposé construction; formal correspondence; academic & professional French; summarising & reformulating; connecteurs logiques soutenus.
**Block 3 · Culture & subtexte** — implicit meaning & inference; press analysis; literature extracts; sociolects & code-switching; negotiation & persuasion; sounding French (discourse fillers, prosody at speed).

### Exam tracks (overlay, not a separate ladder)

Each track = a **task-type syllabus** + **item banks** drawing on the CEFR spine, plus exam-specific strategy micro-lessons. All items are *exam-style originals* — never reproductions (Part 4, issue 5).

| Track | Target users | Task types to cover |
|---|---|---|
| **TEF** (TEF Canada / TEF IRN) | immigration (Canada, France naturalisation) | CO: QCM on dialogues/announcements · CE: QCM on notices/articles · EO: Section A (obtain info by phone) + Section B (convince someone) — *maps directly to Role Play mode* · EE: fait divers continuation + opinion letter |
| **TCF** (TCF Canada / TCF IRN / TCF tout public) | immigration + studies | CO/CE: adaptive QCM banks by level A1→C1 · EO: 3 tasks (interview, interaction with preparation, opinion) · EE: 3 tasks (message, article/letter, argued comparison) |
| **DELF A1–B2 / DALF C1** | studies, residency, proof of level | Per level: CO (recordings + QCM/short answer), CE, PE (letters, essays), PO (entretien dirigé, exercice en interaction, monologue suivi; B2 defence of opinion; C1 synthèse + exposé) |

Exam strategy micro-lessons per track (≈8 each): format walkthrough, timing, scoring rubric explained, model answers with examiner commentary, common traps.

## 1.3 Placement & progression

- The existing `placement.tsx` maps to this spine: a 12–18 item adaptive probe (vocab recognition → audio QCM → produced sentence) that outputs `A0…C1` and sets `profiles.level`. (Currently it returns a fixed result — Part 4, issue 8.)
- Progression rule per unit: unlocked → in progress → **validated** when the unit quiz ≥ 80% *and* its review cards survive one FSRS cycle. Level badge when 85% of units validated. Exam tracks unlock at A2+.

# Part 2 — The Content Plan

## 2.1 Content inventory — what each mode needs, per unit and per level

The unit **bundle** is the production unit. Target sizes (per single unit unless noted):

| Mode (screen) | Content type | Per-unit quantity | Notes / shape (matches existing TS types) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Beginners' Den → Lesson (`den.tsx`, `lesson.tsx`) | `lesson` | 1 | Existing `Lesson` type: tag, title, level, intro, table (+cols), examples 6–10, common errors 3–5, audio scripts 6–10, quiz 4–6 QCM. B1+ adds a short reading passage field. |
| Flashcards (`flashcards.tsx`) | `deck` of `card` | 12–16 cards | `{fr, en, ex}` + `audio` per card + IPA + gender tag for nouns. |
| Voice Flash (`voiceflash.tsx`) | `vf_item` | 6–10 | `{fr, en, key, keyEn}` + image ref. **Blocked on icon/image pipeline** (Part 4, issue 7). |
| Role Play (`roleplay.tsx`) | `roleplay_scenario` | 1 per unit + 3–5 flagship per level | Scripted spine of 4–8 turns `{ai, en, user}` + scene card (role, goal, register) + 2 branch variants per turn + exit criteria. Exam EO tasks (TEF B, TCF interaction, DELF PO) are scenarios with `exam` flag + rubric. |
| Listen & Write / Dictation (`dictation.tsx`) | `dictation_item` | 6–10 sentences | Graded sentence + audio at 2 speeds + accepted-answer variants (elision/punctuation tolerance) + trap annotation (liaison, homophone: *ses/ces/c'est*). |
| Sentence Builder (`sentence.tsx`) | `sb_puzzle` | 4–6 | `{words: [{w,t}], shuffle, target}` + distractor word (B1+) + audio of target. |
| Speaking (`speak.tsx`) | `speak_drill` | 6–8 | Repeat-after-me / shadowing lines with slow+native audio; Sons units instead get **minimal-pair sets** (vin/vent/vont) and rhythm drills. Scoring depends on real STT (Part 4, issue 8) — content must work as "listen & repeat" without scores. |
| Playlist / Player (`player.tsx`, `downloads.tsx`) | `episode` | 1 per unit (60–150 s) + level "series" | Scripted dialogue/monologue: full script with timestamps, EN gloss per line, 3–4 comprehension QCM, key-vocab list feeding review. **This is the main R2 payload** and the whole Downloads feature. |
| Smart Review (`smartreview.tsx`, `review.tsx`) | `review_seed` | 8–12 | Pre-made `ReviewCard`s (WORD/SON/GRAMMAR/CARNET) harvested from the bundle; user-generated ones join via existing `review_items`. |
| Coach chat (`chat.tsx`) | prompt, not rows | — | Runtime LLM via existing `system_prompts` table. The unit bundle supplies **context**: `coach_brief` (150–250 words: what the unit teaches, its traps, its vocab list) injected into the coach prompt. |
| Exam modes | `exam_task` | banks, not per-unit | Per track/section: 20–40 CO items, 20–40 CE items, 10–15 EO scenarios, 10–15 PE prompts with model answers + rubric, per level A2–C1. |

### Volume roadmap (order of magnitude, for cost planning)

| Wave | Scope | Bundles | ~Items | ~Audio clips |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sons + A1 complete (35 units) | 35 | ~2,100 | ~1,600 |
| 2 | A2 complete (31) + placement bank | 31 | ~2,000 | ~1,500 |
| 3 | B1 (32) + TEF/TCF/DELF banks A2–B1 | 32 + banks | ~3,200 | ~2,600 |
| 4 | B2 (28) + exam banks B2 | 28 + banks | ~2,800 | ~2,300 |
| 5 | C1 (20) + DALF C1 + exam banks C1 | 20 + banks | ~2,200 | ~1,800 |

Rule of thumb: **~60 content items and ~45–75 audio clips per unit bundle** (episode counts as many clips if split per line for the player's line-highlighting).

## 2.2 Supabase schema (content plane — new tables)

Additive to the existing control-plane schema; nothing existing changes except a `content_version` key inside `system_config.config`.

```sql
-- One row per curriculum unit (the spine).
create table public.content_units (
  id           text primary key,           -- stable slug: 'a1-08-calendrier-heure'
  level        text not null,              -- A0|A1|A2|B1|B2|C1
  block        text,                       -- e.g. 'b1-recit'
  position     int not null,               -- order within level
  title        text not null,              -- French title (as in curriculum.ts)
  sub          text not null,              -- EN subtitle
  status       text not null default 'draft',  -- draft|review|published
  version      int not null default 1,
  created_at   timestamptz default now()
);

-- Every learnable item, one table, typed payload.
create table public.content_items (
  id           uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  unit_id      text references public.content_units(id),   -- null for exam banks
  type         text not null,   -- lesson|card|vf_item|roleplay_scenario|dictation_item|
                                -- sb_puzzle|speak_drill|episode|review_seed|exam_task|coach_brief
  level        text not null,
  exam         text,            -- null | 'TEF' | 'TCF' | 'DELF' | 'DALF'
  position     int not null default 0,
  payload      jsonb not null,  -- validated against the per-type JSON Schema (§3.3)
  audio_status text not null default 'none',  -- none|pending|ready
  status       text not null default 'draft',
  version      int not null default 1,
  created_at   timestamptz default now()
);
create index on public.content_items (unit_id, type, status);
create index on public.content_items (exam, level) where exam is not null;

-- Audio manifest: one row per generated clip in R2.
create table public.audio_assets (
  id           uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  item_id      uuid not null references public.content_items(id) on delete cascade,
  slot         text not null,   -- which string in the payload: 'card', 'line-3', 'slow', 'native'
  r2_key       text not null unique,  -- audio/fr/{voice}/{item_id}/{slot}.opus
  cdn_url      text not null,         -- public URL via R2 custom domain / CDN
  voice        text not null,         -- 'fr-FR-standard-f1' etc.
  accent       text not null default 'fr-FR',
  speed        text not null default 'native',   -- native|slow
  duration_ms  int,
  bytes        int,
  checksum     text,
  status       text not null default 'pending',  -- pending|ready|failed
  created_at   timestamptz default now()
);

-- Content release pointer (atomic publish + client cache-busting).
create table public.content_releases (
  id           serial primary key,
  version      text not null,          -- '2026.07.1'
  notes        text,
  published_at timestamptz default now()
);

-- RLS: content is world-READABLE only when published; writes via service role only.
alter table public.content_units    enable row level security;
alter table public.content_items    enable row level security;
alter table public.audio_assets     enable row level security;
alter table public.content_releases enable row level security;
create policy "units readable"    on public.content_units    for select using (status = 'published');
create policy "items readable"    on public.content_items    for select using (status = 'published');
create policy "audio readable"    on public.audio_assets     for select using (status = 'ready');
create policy "releases readable" on public.content_releases for select using (true);
```

Why one `content_items` table with `jsonb` payloads instead of 10 typed tables: the app already consumes exactly these TS shapes; payloads are validated by JSON Schema at generation time (§3.4), the client validates with Zod on read, and new modes never need migrations. Postgres GIN indexing on `payload` is available if querying inside payloads ever matters.

## 2.3 Audio pipeline (R2)

**Decision: audio lives in Cloudflare R2, *metadata* lives in Supabase (`audio_assets`).** The app never lists R2; it reads `cdn_url` from rows. R2 specifics:

- **Bucket:** `ealch-audio`, public access via **R2 custom domain** (e.g. `audio.ealch.app`) fronted by Cloudflare CDN + cache rules (immutable, 1-year TTL — keys are content-addressed so cache invalidation is never needed).
- **Key convention:** `audio/fr/{voice}/{item_id}/{slot}[-slow].opus` — deterministic, so regeneration overwrites and the checksum row updates.
- **Format:** Opus 32–48 kbps mono (speech-optimised, ~1/4 the size of MP3 at equal quality; supported by expo-audio/AV on both platforms). Keep MP3 fallback only if a target device problem is proven.
- **Two speeds** for dictation/speak slots: `native` and `slow` (0.75× generated natively by the TTS, not client-side pitch-shifted).
- **Worker flow:** generation script inserts `content_items` → enqueues TTS jobs → TTS worker (Edge Function or local script) calls the configured provider (config already names `fishAudio`/`fish-1`), uploads to R2 via S3-compatible API, inserts `audio_assets`, flips `audio_status='ready'`.
- **Downloads feature:** a level-pack manifest = `select r2_key, bytes from audio_assets join content_items … where level='A1'` — gives the Downloads screen real sizes and a real fetch list.
- **Fallback:** the app's existing device-TTS remains the offline/failed-asset fallback — this is already how every screen works today, so shipping content *before* audio is done is safe (`audio_status` gates the UI).

**One accent for v1** (`fr-FR` neutral/Parisian, one female + one male voice). Per-accent variants (`profiles.accent`) multiply audio cost linearly — defer (Part 4, issue 6).

## 2.4 Delivery to the app (ContentService — the missing piece)

1. On launch (and on foreground, reusing the config refresh path): read `content_releases` latest version; if newer than cached, sync.
2. Sync = pull `content_units` + `content_items` (published, for the user's level ± 1) into AsyncStorage/SQLite; store `version`.
3. `src/content/*.ts` seed files become the **zero-config fallback** (exactly the pattern `config.ts` already uses for remote config) — app works with no network and no Supabase forever.
4. Client Zod-validates every payload on read; invalid rows are skipped, never crash a screen.

# Part 3 — Content Generation (the prompt system)

## 3.1 Architecture: one master prompt + per-type job specs

One **master system prompt** (below) fixes persona, pedagogy, French-quality rules, and output discipline. Each generation run appends a **job spec**: the unit row, the item `type`, its JSON Schema, quantities, and the recycled-vocab list. A runner script (Node) loops units × types, calls the LLM (config already names `claude-sonnet-5` as the `content` model), validates output against the schema, and inserts rows with `status='review'`.

Store the master prompt in the existing `system_prompts` table (`key='content-gen'`, versioned) so prompt iterations are auditable — the table was built for exactly this.

## 3.2 The Master Prompt (v1 — ready to use)

```text
You are the Ealch Content Engine — a native French pedagogue (agrégé de FLE,
15 years teaching CEFR-aligned French, DELF/DALF examiner-trained) who writes
learning content for Ealch, a speaking-first French app for adult learners.

You will receive a JOB SPEC (JSON) containing: the curriculum unit (id, level,
title, sub, teaching goal), the item TYPE to produce, the exact JSON SCHEMA the
output must satisfy, the QUANTITY, a RECYCLE list of previously taught
vocabulary, and optionally an EXAM tag (TEF | TCF | DELF | DALF).

════════ NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES ════════

LEVEL DISCIPLINE
- Every French string must be producible by a learner AT the unit's CEFR level
  using only grammar/vocab from this unit and earlier units. When in doubt, go
  simpler. A0/A1: present tense, high-frequency lexicon (top ~1000 words),
  sentences ≤ 9 words. A2: + passé composé, futur proche, ≤ 14 words.
  B1: + imparfait, futur simple, conditionnel, subjonctif triggers taught so far.
  B2/C1: natural native French, register control required.
- Reuse at least 30% of the RECYCLE list across the batch. Never introduce more
  than 8 genuinely new lexical items per batch outside the unit's target list.

FRENCH QUALITY
- Impeccable French: correct gender, agreement, elision, contractions (au, du,
  des), and punctuation with French typography: « guillemets », apostrophes ('),
  espaces before ! ? : ; and accents ALWAYS (including capitals: É, À, Ç).
- Every noun taught carries its article (un/une/le/la) — never bare nouns.
- Register must match the scene: vous with strangers/officials, tu among friends.
  Mark any familiar/slang item explicitly in the payload field provided for it.
- English glosses are natural English, not word-for-word calques.

AUDIO AWARENESS (everything you write will be spoken by TTS)
- Every string destined for audio must read aloud unambiguously: expand numerals
  and symbols in a dedicated audio_script field when the display text contains
  digits, €, %, or abbreviations ("2,50 €" → "deux euros cinquante").
- For dictation items, deliberately include the unit's listening traps
  (liaisons, homophones, silent endings) and enumerate accepted answer variants.

PEDAGOGY
- Examples teach one thing at a time; common-error entries must be errors real
  anglophone/hispanophone/sinophone learners actually make, with a one-line WHY.
- Quiz distractors must be plausible (real forms, wrong context) — never jokes.
- Roleplay: the AI speaks first; each user turn has a clear communicative goal;
  include the polite-failure path (user doesn't understand → AI rephrases slower).

EXAM ITEMS (when EXAM tag present)
- Produce ORIGINAL items in the authentic FORMAT of the exam (task type, timing,
  scoring rubric) but NEVER reproduce, paraphrase, or imitate specific published
  exam papers or copyrighted sample items. Invent fresh scenarios each time.
- Include the marking rubric and one model answer with 2-3 examiner comments.
- Label every item with exam, section (CO|CE|EO|EE), and CEFR level.

OUTPUT DISCIPLINE
- Output ONLY a JSON array of objects that validate against the provided SCHEMA.
  No markdown, no commentary, no trailing text.
- All user-visible instruction strings in the payload exist in both fr and en
  fields as the schema dictates. Do not add fields the schema doesn't define.
- Self-check before emitting: schema-valid? level-appropriate? French flawless?
  audio_script present wherever digits/symbols appear? If any check fails,
  regenerate that object.
```

## 3.3 Job spec template (sent per run)

```json
{
  "unit": { "id": "b1-01-imparfait-vs-pc", "level": "B1", "block": "b1-recit",
            "title": "Imparfait vs passé composé",
            "sub": "background vs event — the storytelling pair",
            "goal": "Learner narrates a past anecdote choosing tenses correctly." },
  "type": "dictation_item",
  "quantity": 8,
  "recycle": ["hier", "pendant", "soudain", "se lever", "en retard", "…"],
  "exam": null,
  "schema": { "$ref": "schemas/dictation_item.schema.json" }
}
```

## 3.4 Per-type JSON Schemas (the contract)

One JSON Schema file per `type`, kept in-repo (`ealch-v2/content-schemas/*.schema.json`) and mirrored as Zod on the client. They encode the existing TS types plus audio slots. Summary of required fields:

| type | payload requires |
|---|---|
| `lesson` | tag, title, level, intro, table{cols,cells[]}, examples[{fr,en}], errors[{wrong,right,why}], audio_scripts[], quiz[{q,opts[4],correct}], reading?{fr,en} (B1+) |
| `card` | fr, en, ex, ipa, pos, gender?, audio_script |
| `vf_item` | fr, en, key, keyEn, image_ref, audio_script |
| `roleplay_scenario` | scene{role,setting,goal,register}, level, turns[{ai,en,user_goal,user_sample,branches[2]}], exit_criteria, exam?{track,section,rubric,model_answer} |
| `dictation_item` | text, audio_script, accepted[], traps[], translation_en |
| `sb_puzzle` | words[{w,t}], target, distractors[] (B1+), audio_script, translation_en |
| `speak_drill` | kind(repeat\|shadow\|minimal_pair), lines[{fr,en,audio_script}], focus (e.g. 'nasales'), pair?{a,b,contrast} |
| `episode` | title, duration_target_s, script[{speaker,fr,en,t_hint}], vocab[{fr,en}], questions[{q,opts,correct}], summary_fr, summary_en |
| `review_seed` | card_type(WORD\|SON\|GRAMMAR\|CARNET), prompt, answer, source_item_ref |
| `exam_task` | track, section, level, instructions_fr, instructions_en, stimulus, questions?/prompt?, rubric, model_answer, examiner_notes[], timing_s |
| `coach_brief` | summary, target_structures[], vocab[], traps[], sample_corrections[{learner,fixed,why}] |

## 3.5 QA pipeline (content is not trusted until it passes)

1. **Machine gate (runner script):** JSON-Schema validation → French typography lint (accents on capitals, « » pairs, NBSP before `!?:;`) → level heuristics (sentence length, banned-tense regexes per level: e.g. no `-rais` at A1) → recycle-rate check → duplicate detection against existing rows.
2. **LLM cross-check:** a *different* model/prompt ("You are a hostile DELF examiner; find every error") reviews each batch and outputs a defect list; items with defects regenerate automatically (max 2 loops).
3. **Human gate:** rows land as `status='review'`; a native/near-native reviewer spot-checks a fixed 15% sample per batch in a simple admin view (or a Supabase table view). A batch passing sample review flips wholesale to `published`; a failing batch is rejected wholesale. Non-negotiable for exam model answers and all Sons/A1 content (beginners can't self-correct bad input).
4. **Audio gate:** post-TTS spot-listen of 5% per batch (wrong liaison or number reading is common in TTS); the `audio_script` field exists precisely to control this.

# Part 4 — Issues found that will break this if not resolved

Ranked: blockers first.

1. **🔴 No stable content IDs in the app.** Units are addressed by array index (`'sons-2'`, `extendedLesson['a1-3']`, `a2Subs` index-aligned to `currA2`). The moment content comes from a DB, index-keying collapses (reordering/inserting a unit corrupts references and users' saved progress). **Decide slugs first** (`a1-08-calendrier-heure`), migrate `curriculum.ts` and the store's progress keys to them *before* any DB work.
2. **🔴 Supabase schema has no content tables** and the referenced `ContentService` doesn't exist. Part 2.2/2.4 designs them, but note the dependency: nothing in Part 3 can be *fed to the app* until this lands. Generation can still start earlier — output can sit in the DB unpublished.
3. **🔴 R2 ↔ Supabase are two systems with no glue.** The app reads Supabase; audio lives in R2. Without the `audio_assets` manifest table + deterministic key convention (§2.3), you get orphaned files, broken URLs, and no way to build download packs. Also decide now: **public bucket via custom domain** (recommended: content is not secret, enables CDN caching and offline downloads) vs signed URLs (breaks offline downloads, adds an Edge Function on every play). Note R2 has no per-object ACL worth relying on for this use case — public-read bucket + unguessable-enough keys is the pragmatic call.
4. **🔴 LLM French cannot be trusted raw.** Single-pass generation will produce gender errors, wrong registers, and anglicisms — at A0/A1 the learner cannot detect them, which is pedagogically toxic. The QA pipeline (§3.5) is not optional; budget for the human sample review, especially Sons/A1 and exam model answers.
5. **🔴 Exam content copyright.** TEF (Le français des affaires/CCI Paris), TCF and DELF/DALF (France Éducation international) materials are copyrighted; exam names are their marks. Generating *original items in the same format* is standard practice and fine; copying/paraphrasing published papers is not. Also add a visible disclaimer ("not affiliated with/endorsed by FEI or CCI Paris") — needed for app-store truthfulness too. Exam formats change (TCF revised recently; TEF Canada expression tasks updated) — tag every exam item with a `format_version` so a format change doesn't silently invalidate banks.
6. **🟠 Accent feature multiplies audio cost.** `profiles.accent` default 'Parisienne' implies variants. Each additional accent ≈ +100% audio generation and storage for spoken slots. v1: one neutral fr-FR accent, keep the field, populate variants later only for high-value slots (episodes). B2 Block 4 handles accents as *recognition* content, which needs only a handful of clips.
7. **🟠 Voice Flash can't scale.** `VfIcon` is a closed union of 5 hardcoded icons. Scaling to hundreds of items needs an image strategy: (a) extend the icon set (limited), (b) an illustration/emoji mapping per item, or (c) generated/stock images stored in R2 alongside audio. Until decided, cap vf_item generation to the existing icon vocabulary — the schema's `image_ref` field is designed so content doesn't have to be regenerated when the pipeline arrives.
8. **🟠 Speaking & placement scoring are fake** (audit findings B3: STT always returns success; placement returns a fixed result). Content strategy must assume **no reliable pronunciation scoring at launch**: speak_drills are written to work as honest listen-and-repeat, and placement items are QCM/tap-based (self-contained) rather than speech-scored. When real STT lands, the same content gains scoring without regeneration.
9. **🟠 Offline-first vs content volume.** Waves 1–5 total ~12k items and ~10k clips (~40–80 MB audio per level in Opus). Syncing *everything* to AsyncStorage will hurt; sync text for level ± 1 only, and audio strictly on-demand/downloads. AsyncStorage has practical size limits on Android — plan for SQLite (expo-sqlite) if text payloads exceed a few MB.
10. **🟡 i18n multiplication.** The app offers 7 UI languages, but all content glosses are English-only. Translating glosses ×6 multiplies generation and review cost. v1: FR content + EN glosses only (matching current app reality); the schema keeps glosses in named fields (`en`) so adding `es`/`zh` later is additive columns in payloads, not regeneration.
11. **🟡 `system_prompts` RLS is world-readable including inactive versions** (audit C7) — the master content prompt would be public IP. Restrict to `active = true` or keep the content-gen prompt out of the client-readable table (it's only used server-side anyway).
12. **🟡 TTS provider not actually wired.** Config names `fishAudio`/`fish-1` but no integration exists. The pipeline (§2.3) isolates this behind the worker, so provider choice (Fish Audio vs Azure vs ElevenLabs vs OpenAI TTS) is swappable; pick based on French liaison quality + cost per character — run a 20-sentence bake-off with dictation traps as the test set before committing to ~10k clips.
13. **🟡 Cost sanity check.** ~10k clips × ~8 s avg ≈ 22 audio-hours. At typical 2026 TTS pricing this is roughly $50–$400 total depending on provider (character-priced) — fine. LLM generation: ~12k items ≈ 15–25M output tokens ≈ low hundreds of dollars on a Sonnet-class model including QA loops — fine, but the *human review time* (issue 4) is the real cost line.

---

# Part 5 — Suggested sequence (planning summary, no build implied)

1. **Decide the blockers:** slugs (issue 1) · R2 public-domain strategy (issue 3) · one-accent v1 (issue 6) · exam disclaimer text (issue 5).
2. **Land the content plane:** schema §2.2 migration · seed `content_units` from `curriculum.ts` + Part 1 B1/B2/C1 lists · ContentService + fallback (§2.4).
3. **Prove the pipe with one bundle end-to-end:** generate `a1-01-salutations` full bundle → QA → publish → TTS → R2 → app plays it. Everything after this is repetition.
4. **Wave 1 (Sons + A1)** with full QA; run the TTS bake-off inside this wave.
5. **Waves 2–5** per §2.1, exam banks starting Wave 3.
